clue.text: Days of old power studied for big corporation

definitions.note: corporation is an old jokey word for a paunch

parts.note: the Middle Ages are the medieval era, days long gone
P is the physics symbol for power
to read a subject is to study it at university

explanation.surface: A historical power base is analysed in terms of a giant modern company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' looks like a business, but it is an old word for a large belly.
explanation.definitionFit: A paunch that develops in one's forties or fifties is a large belly, the jocular sense of corporation.

clue.text: Idiots upset MP in reshuffle

indicators.note: a cabinet reshuffle moves people around, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Fools disturb a Member of Parliament during a cabinet reshuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Muppets is British slang for foolish people, taken from the puppet show.

clue.text: More bananas showing a higher number of speckles

definitions.meaning: bananas is slang for crazy, so more bananas means crazier

definitions.text: showing a higher number of speckles
definitions.meaning: more covered in spots or dots

explanation.definitionFit: Dotty means slightly mad and also spotted, so the comparative fits both crazier and more spotted.

clue.text: Famous Italian represented cardinal on video

indicators.note: the letters are presented again in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A churchman appears on film, portrayed as a celebrated Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: The Renaissance painter of the Mona Lisa is among the best-known Italians in history.

clue.text: Lilac rim on yam's inside reveals bitterness

indicators.note: the letters wanted sit within the run of words lilac rim on yam's

explanation.surface: Looking at a lilac-rimmed yam somehow uncovers resentment.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrimony is bitter, angry feeling between people, a synonym of bitterness.

clue.text: In a bad way in Spain, very unwell, variable

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain
ill means unwell
Y is a standard algebraic symbol for a variable

explanation.surface: Someone holidaying in Spain is very poorly and up and down.
explanation.definitionFit: Evilly is an adverb meaning wickedly, which is acting in a bad way.

clue.text: Irish pool staff, small and large, getting into party drink and food

indicators.note: the run of pieces goes inside the drink, entering it

parts.note: punch is a mixed drink served in a bowl at parties
a lough is an Irish lake
to man is to staff
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Irish workers of every size crash a party for drinks and snacks.
explanation.walkthrough: A ploughman's lunch is a British pub meal of bread, cheese and pickle.
explanation.definitionFit: This cold pub plate of bread, cheese and pickle is a meal, so it is food.

clue.text: Eastern Fleet being shelled will swallow tax boost

indicators.note: the shelled word takes the tax inside it
the word fleet loses its outer letters like a shelled nut

parts.note: VAT is value added tax

explanation.surface: A navy in the east is stripped and must absorb a tax rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleet' and 'boost' suggest a navy and morale; 'being shelled' sounds like bombardment but means removing the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To elevate is to raise or lift up, a synonym of boost as a verb.

clue.text: Stood for flipping parade — tone-deaf taking part

indicators.note: the letters found are turned round, read right to left
the answer is a part of the run parade tone-deaf

explanation.surface: A tuneless marching band ruins a parade, to the anger of all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking part' picks DETONED from paraDE TONEDeaf, and 'flipping' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To denote is to signify or represent, so denoted means represented, or stood for.

clue.text: Rip up root for replanting, leaving petals in a bowl?

indicators.note: putting the letters back in the ground in a new order

explanation.surface: A gardener tears up a root to replant it, leaving petals behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Pot-pourri is a scented mix of dried petals, typically kept in a dish.

clue.text: Poem about place of fantasy …

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem
on means concerning, about

explanation.surface: A poem concerning some imaginary realm.
explanation.walkthrough: Odeon is a chain of British cinemas, and a cinema shows fantasy.
explanation.definitionFit: A cinema is a venue where filmed fantasies play, so it is a place of make-believe.

clue.text: … it is featured in retro street musical

indicators.note: the word it appears inside the reversed street
retro means backwards, so the street abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: AVE is short for avenue, a street

explanation.surface: A street-set musical with a nostalgic style.
explanation.definitionFit: This Lloyd Webber stage show about Eva Perón is a well-known musical.

clue.text: Venomous African country midge bites unknown number

parts.note: Mali is a country in West Africa

indicators.note: the insect holds the number in its jaws

parts.note: a gnat is a midge
N is the algebraic symbol for an indefinite number

explanation.surface: A poisonous insect in an African nation bites many people.
explanation.definitionFit: Malignant means spiteful and harmful, a synonym of venomous in its figurative sense.

clue.text: Rough National Trust walk ahead

indicators.note: the walk goes in front of the other piece

parts.note: a stride is a long step in walking
NT is the National Trust, a British heritage charity

explanation.surface: A tough hike on National Trust land lies ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Strident means harsh and grating in sound, so rough in the sense of jarring.

clue.text: Threaten prankster with death

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous creature
end means death

explanation.surface: Someone menaces a practical joker with being killed.
explanation.definitionFit: To impend is to loom or hang over menacingly, so to threaten.

clue.text: Kind of French clubs with dodgy casino Romeo inhabits

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

indicators.note: the letter lives inside the scrambled casino
dodgy means unreliable, so the casino letters are scrambled

parts.note: R is Romeo in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A French club with a crooked casino is home to a lover.
explanation.walkthrough: Corsica is a French island, so its people are a kind of French.
explanation.definitionFit: Corsica belongs to France, so a native of the island is one variety of French person.

clue.text: Sack's covering penny or something in river

indicators.note: the raids enclose the penny

parts.note: to sack a town is to raid it, so sacks are raids

explanation.surface: A sack holds a penny or some other thing found in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapids are a fast, turbulent stretch of water in a river.

clue.text: There's always a lapse before it's read

definitions.text: There's always a lapse before it's read

parts.words: There's always a lapse before it's read
parts.note: the formal order to disperse is only read out after discipline has lapsed into disorder

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lapse' suggests a pause before a book is read; here it is a lapse into unruliness that prompts a stern warning.
explanation.definitionFit: This stern warning was historically read to unruly crowds, and figuratively to anyone misbehaving.

clue.text: One has faith one will go far

definitions.text: One has faith one will go far

parts.words: One has faith one will go far
parts.note: a devout traveller journeys a long way to a shrine

explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like confidence in a promising career; read literally it is a believer who travels a long way.
explanation.definitionFit: A religious traveller to a holy place is a person of faith making a long journey.

clue.text: Take in case of broken limb being blue

parts.note: to down a drink is to take it in
a plaster cast encases a broken arm or leg

explanation.surface: Taking in someone's plastered fracture makes them feel low.
explanation.definitionFit: Downcast means low-spirited, and blue is a common word for sad.

clue.text: Retail confused lies about English artist's place in Paris?

indicators.note: the mixed letters lie around the other piece
the letters of retail are mixed up

explanation.surface: A muddled shopkeeper tells untruths about an English painter's studio in France.
explanation.definitionFit: An atelier is a studio or workshop, the French word for an artist's working room.

clue.text: House-keeping? It could be a flat occupation

definitions.meaning: keeping a house as a renter, holding it for a term

definitions.text: It could be a flat occupation
definitions.meaning: occupying an apartment as a tenant

explanation.walkthrough: 'House-keeping' suggests cleaning, and 'flat occupation' a dull job; both mean living in rented property.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenancy is the holding of rented property, whether a house or an apartment.

clue.text: Second bird, one from America originally

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
a hawk is a bird of prey

explanation.surface: A second bird species turns out to have been American at first.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mohawk are an indigenous people of North America, original inhabitants of the land.

clue.text: About fifty, one is plain absent-minded

indicators.note: the plain word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: obvious means plain, clear
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone about fifty is clearly getting forgetful.
explanation.definitionFit: Oblivious means unaware of one's surroundings, close to forgetful or absent-minded.

clue.text: Catch up with rest of fiction (popular)

parts.note: a lie is a falsehood, a fiction
in means fashionable, popular

explanation.surface: Taking a break from popular novels to catch up.
explanation.definitionFit: A long morning in bed is a way to recover lost sleep, catching up on rest.

clue.text: Personal accident cover, with strings attached

definitions.text: Personal accident cover, with strings attached

parts.words: Personal accident cover, with strings attached
parts.note: an insurance policy with conditions read as a garment that shields the body from spills and ties on

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as an insurance policy with conditions; it is really a kitchen garment that ties on with strings.
explanation.definitionFit: This tied garment protects the wearer's clothes from splashes and spills while cooking.

clue.text: Last act of Jesus — Son, in case uncertain?

indicators.note: letters whose order is unsure are rearranged

explanation.surface: A puzzled question on whether the final deed of Christ was the Son's, just in case.
explanation.definitionFit: In Christian belief Christ's rising into heaven was his final act on earth.

clue.text: Male detective with hound following Joe Bloggs?

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
dick is slang for a private detective
and means with, together
to harry is to hound or harass

explanation.surface: A man and a private eye with a dog trail an ordinary bloke.
explanation.walkthrough: Joe Bloggs is the British name for a typical ordinary person.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means any ordinary person at all, like Joe Bloggs, the British everyman.
